blocks.text: Stoichiometry is the branch of chemistry that gives the quantitative relationship between reactants and products in a balanced chemical equation. With the mole, Avogadro's number, molar mass, molar volume and molar concentration, quantitative relationships between reactants and products can be established from balanced equations. Six types of relationship can be studied: mole-mole, mass-mass, volume-volume, mole-mass, mole-volume and mass-volume. To use them, the information hidden in a balanced equation must be read. For N2(g) + 3H2(g) gives 2NH3(g): one mole of N2 reacts with three moles of H2 to form two moles of NH3; one molecule of N2 reacts with three molecules of H2 to form two molecules of NH3; 22.4 dm3 of N2 reacts with 67.2 dm3 of H2 to form 44.8 dm3 of NH3; and 28.0 g of N2 reacts with 6 g of H2 to form 34.0 g of NH3.

blocks.title: Keep in mind
blocks.text: Stoichiometric calculations assume that all the reactants are completely converted into products, that the laws of conservation of mass and definite proportions are obeyed, and that no side reaction occurs.

blocks.alt: Five rounded boxes stacked vertically and joined by downward arrows: yellow (mass of known solid, volume of known gas or molar concentration of known solution), green (calculate moles of the known using the relevant formula), red (ratio of known and unknown from the balanced equation), blue (moles of the unknown using the relevant formula) and orange (convert moles of the unknown to mass, volume or concentration).
blocks.caption: Approach to do stoichiometric calculations (original drawing after the scheme printed on p82 of the textbook).
blocks.long_description: Box 1: Mass of known solid or volume of a known gas, or molar concentration of known solution. Box 2: Calculate number of moles of known solid or volume of a known gas, or molar concentration of known solution using the relevant formula. Box 3: Find the ratio of the known and the unknown reactant or product from the balanced chemical equation. Box 4: Calculate the number of moles of the unknown reactant or product using the relevant formula. Box 5: Convert the number of moles of the unknown to mass, volume, or concentration of the substance.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed box 3 reads 'unknow'; the word is unknown.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Sample Problem 4.11: the question gives 3.3 mol of N2 (not 3.6 moles); 3.3 mol N2 needs 3 x 3.3 = 9.9 mol H2. Sample Problem 4.12: 32.0 / 159.6 = 0.200 mol Fe2O3, so Al = 2 x 0.200 = 0.401 mol and the mass of Al = 0.401 x 27 = 10.8 g, not 1.08 g.
